title: Morphometry of the Wadi Na'man catchment east of Makkah from NASADEM
data: NASADEM_HGT version 001 by NASA JPL (2020): 1 arc-second (about 30 m) elevations from the SRTM flight of February 2000, in whole metres above the EGM96 geoid, tiles n21e039 and n21e040.
method: Read a 65 × 65 km window (EPSG:32637, x 595000 to 660000, y 2325000 to 2390000) and reprojected it to 30 m cells.
Filled depressions by priority flood (Wang and Liu 2006) and derived D8 flow direction and accumulation.

Outlet on the OpenStreetMap line of Wadi Na'man at 40.0320° E, 21.3341° N, moved downstream to the first cell draining 100 km²; delineated the catchment and checked that it does not touch the window edge.
Streams: cells draining 1 km² or more, ordered by Strahler, recomputed at 0.5 and 2 km².
limits: These are shape parameters, not discharges, flood levels or a hydrology study, and they are not for plan approval. The NASADEM user guide (NASA JPL, 2020) gives the SRTM requirement as 16 m absolute vertical error at 90% and a global average absolute height error of about 6.8 m; the model is a radar surface of February 2000 in whole metres. The network and its density follow the threshold: at 0.5 km² the highest order becomes 6 and the density 1.11 km/km²; at 2 km² the order is 4 and the density 0.61.
